summary: The algorithmic language designed by a joint European and American committee. It was rarely used to build commercial programs, but its block structure and the way it was specified shaped Pascal, C and nearly every language after them.

image.alt: Cover of a 1965 ALGOL language manual

events.note: ALGOL 58 is designed at a committee meeting at ETH Zurich.

events.label: ALGOL 60
events.note: The ALGOL 60 report, edited by Peter Naur, defines the language most people mean by ALGOL.

events.label: Revised report
events.note: A revised ALGOL 60 report is published.

events.label: ALGOL 68
events.note: A far larger successor that is poorly received.

note: No official end. Its block structure shaped Pascal, C and most languages after it.
